properties.vocals: Lead vocals were provided primarily by Freddie Mercury, whose powerful, versatile voice combined a baritonal chest with strong tenor and falsetto/head registers, enabling multi-octave phrasing and operatic runs; Brian May and Roger Taylor provided distinctive multi-part harmonies and backing vocals, giving Queen their signature layered choral sound.
properties.biography: Brian May and Roger Taylor played together in the band Smile. Freddie Mercury, a fan of Smile, joined the musicians in 1970 and suggested the name "Queen." John Deacon completed the classic lineup in 1971. The band released their self-titled debut in 1973, and after early albums that showed progressive and heavy influences, they broke through internationally with A Night at the Opera (1975) and the epochal single "Bohemian Rhapsody." Through the late 1970s and early 1980s Queen became one of the preeminent stadium rock acts, known for layered studio production, diverse genre shifts, and commanding live performances culminating in the celebrated Live Aid set in 1985. Freddie Mercury's AIDS diagnosis in 1987 and his death in 1991 marked the end of the original era; the band released one posthumous Mercury-fronted album (Made in Heaven, 1995). John Deacon retired in 1997; Brian May and Roger Taylor have since performed and toured with guest vocalists under the Queen banner.
properties.known_for: Layered vocal harmonies, theatrical live shows, genre-blending songwriting and stadium-ready anthems like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "We Are the Champions."
properties.description: Queen is a British rock band formed in London in 1970 by Freddie Mercury, Brian May and Roger Taylor, with John Deacon joining in 1971. The band blended progressive rock, hard rock and heavy metal origins with pop, arena and operatic elements to create theatrical, multi-layered recordings and stadium-ready anthems. They achieved international success with albums such as A Night at the Opera (1975) and singles like "Bohemian Rhapsody," "We Will Rock You" and "We Are the Champions." Queen's live performance at Live Aid (1985) is widely celebrated; Freddie Mercury's death in 1991 was a pivotal moment for the group. Brian May and Roger Taylor have continued to perform under the Queen name in various configurations (notably Queen + Paul Rodgers and Queen + Adam Lambert). Queen's catalogue, distinctive vocal harmonies, and showmanship have made them one of the world's best-selling and most influential rock acts.
properties.cultural_impact: Queen has had a profound global cultural impact: tens to hundreds of millions of records sold (estimates 250	600 million), songs that became international sporting anthems, a landmark Live Aid performance, major industry awards (Brit Award for Outstanding Contribution, Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Songwriters Hall of Fame, Grammy Lifetime Achievement) and renewed mainstream attention from the 2018 biopic Bohemian Rhapsody; their production techniques and theatricality influenced music video practice and stadium rock presentation worldwide.
properties.performance_style: Highly theatrical and meticulously produced live shows featuring Freddie Mercury's charismatic frontmanship, large-scale audience participation, layered vocal harmonies, and a mix of intimate and stadium-sized numbers across multiple genres.

properties.biography: Fall Out Boy formed in 2001 in the Chicago suburbs when friends and local-scene musicians combined songwriting and punk roots into a more pop-focused sound. Core members Patrick Stump (lead vocals, guitar), Pete Wentz (bass, principal lyricist), Joe Trohman (lead guitar) and Andy Hurley (drums) solidified the lineup early in the band's career. They built an early fanbase with independent releases and relentless touring; their 2003 debut Take This to Your Grave established them within the emo/pop-punk scene. Mainstream breakthrough came with 2005's From Under the Cork Tree, followed by major-label success, a brief hiatus in 2009, and a high-profile return in 2013 with Save Rock and Roll. Across multiple albums they balanced catchy, radio-friendly songwriting with emotionally frank lyrics, helping bring emo and pop-punk into mainstream popular culture.

properties.biography: Journey formed in San Francisco in 1973 under manager Herbie Herbert, originally intended as a backing group for Bay Area acts and featuring Santana alumni Neal Schon and Gregg Rolie among others. Early records explored jazz-fusion territory but failed to sell; pressure from Columbia Records and the recruitment of singer Steve Perry in 1977 steered the band toward a more radio-friendly, melodic rock/AOR sound. With Jonathan Cain joining on keyboards in 1980, Journey achieved its greatest commercial success with albums such as Infinity (1978), Departure (1980), Escape (1981) and Frontiers (1983). The band produced multiple enduring hits and became a staple of stadium and arena rock in the 1980s. Personnel shifts, hiatuses and reformations followed through the 1990s and 2000s; in 2007 Arnel Pineda joined as lead vocalist after being discovered on YouTube. Journey has continued touring and releasing albums into the 21st century.

properties.description: Journey is an American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1973 by former Santana members and other Bay Area musicians. They evolved from a jazz-fusion backing group into a commercially successful arena and melodic rock band after recruiting lead singer Steve Perry in 1977. Journey scored global hits in the late 1970s and 1980s — notably "Don't Stop Believin'", "Open Arms", "Faithfully" and "Separate Ways" — and became one of the definitive AOR/arena-rock acts, combining soaring tenor vocals, polished production, synthesizer-driven keyboards and guitar virtuosity. The band has undergone numerous lineup changes, continued releasing albums across decades, and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2017.
properties.cultural_impact: Journey produced some of the most enduring anthem rock songs of the late 20th century; "Don't Stop Believin'" became a perennial cultural touchstone used in films, TV (notably The Sopranos finale and Glee), sports arenas and karaoke worldwide. The band's polished AOR sound helped define 1980s arena rock and power ballad conventions. Their commercial ubiquity, licensing of music for advertising and video games, and eventual Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in 2017 underscore a lasting mainstream impact.
